Allegations in brief are that, the accused was a public servant and working as the Assistant Executive Engineer, KSRTC Head Office at Shanthi Nagara, Bengaluru City. The check period applicable to him is 25.08.1989 to 29.03.2014. During the said period, the accused had accumulated the total assets worth Rs.61,45,944/- (29.84%) disproportionate to his known sources of an income worth Rs.2,05,90,607.00. The accused has created and forged the documents with an intention to Karnataka Lokayuktha Bangalore City ... vs K B Ramakrishna Reddy on 31 October, 2025 cheat. Having failed to give the satisfactory accounts therefor, the accused has committed the afore- referred offences.

After taking cognizance of the offence, the case was got registered by this Court. The presence of the accused was secured. He was represented by a counsel and got enlarged on the bail. After the complying the requirement under Section 207 of Cr.P.C., this court has framed the charge against the accused for offences 4 Spl. C.C.456/2017 punishable under Section 13(1)(e) read with Section 13(2) of the PC Act and Sections 465 & 471 of IPC, read over and explained the same in the language known to him. He pleaded not guilty, but claims to be tried. Hence, the trial of the case was fixed. To prove its allegations, the prosecution has examined 17 witnesses as PW1 to 17 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to P130. After closure of the prosecution evidence, and getting compliance of Section 437(A), the accused has been examined under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Having denied the incriminating circumstances appearing against him in the evidence of the prosecution witnesses to be false, the accused has adduced the evidence as DW1 apart examining his 4 witnesses as Dw.2 to 5. He has got marked documents as per Ex.D1 to 20 in support of his defence that, he is an innocent. Heard arguments from the learned Public Prosecutor and the defence arguments with reference to the written arguments from the learned counsel for the accused. After going through the record, the following points would arise for the consideration. Does the prosecution prove beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused was a public 5 Spl. C.C.456/2017 servant?

Does the prosecution prove beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused had accumulated the assets worth Rs.61,45,944/- (29.84%) disproportionate to his known sources of an income during his check period and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 13(1)(e) r/w Section 13(2) of the PC Act, 1988? 3 Does the prosecution prove beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused had dishonestly and fraudulently prepared and submitted the bills worth Rs.62,28,480/- and Rs.25,95,000/- respectively by using them to be genuine bills and thereby committed offences punishable under Sections 465 and 471 of IPC? Point No.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative and 3 in the negative for the following : REASONS Point No.1 : It is not in dispute that, the accused was working as the Assistant Executive Engineer in the head office of KSRTC at Shanthi Nagara, Bengaluru as on the date of the raid. He was a public servant as defined 6 Spl. C.C.456/2017 under Section 2(c) of the PC Act. The Lokayukta Police have conducted the raid upon the house and other places of the accused on 29.03.2014. In view of these admitted facts, the status of the accused as a public servant does not warrant the further discussion. Whereas, the accused denies the said allegations as baseless. He asserts that, he is an innocent and has not committed any offence as alleged. His counsel has advanced the oral arguments with reference to his written arguments. According to him, the accused is an innocent and the Police have falsely registered the present case based on an inflated the assets rather than, filing the 'B' report for want of evidence to constitute the ingredients of alleged offences. Generally, and even as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Krishna Reddy Vs. State by the Dy.S.P., Hyderbad reported as (1992) 4 SCC 45 and Vasanth Rao Huge Vs. State of M. P reported as (2017) 14 8 Spl. C.C.456/2017 SCC 442, the burden is on the prosecution to prove the offence of criminal misconduct, rather than expecting the accused to prove his defence. However, in the case of Subhas Kharate Vs. State of M. P reported as 2000 KLJ 1178 and AIR 1973 SC 2773 in the case of Kali Ram Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh, it was held that, once the prosecution discharges its burden, giving scope to raise the statutory presumption, the onus shifts upon the accused to rebut such presumption based on the preponderance of probabilities. Also referred AIR 1979 SC 1455 in the case of Mansingh Vs. Delhi Administration. With this background, the offence in question against the accused needs to decide with reference to the material evidence on his assets, expenditure and the income. Rathnamma under the sale deed dtd: 09.01.2004 as per the sale deed at Ex.P78. But, in his 13(A) schedule statement, the accused states that, his wife has purchased the site out of her savings from the tailoring business and the rent from the house in site No.6. Admittedly, she was a house wife and has not been examined in this case to prove her source of income. It is not in dispute that, a sewing machine was found in the house of the accused at the time of search by the Police. The accused has not placed any material to prove the independent source for his wife to save prior to 2004. If really, she was earning from the tailoring to the extent of purchasing the property, she should have certainly maintained the account to that extent as rightly argued by the learned Public Prosecutor. Thus, in the absence of such evidence, mere possessing the sewing machine in the house for the personal purpose would not be a ground to presume the income. 14 Spl. Chinnappa Reddy being the adopted father of his wife has purchased the site in her name. But, there is no even an iota of document or supporting circumstance to prove it. That apart, his wife was not the owner of site No.6 as on 09.01.2004 prior to its sale to the accused. Rather, she sold this site to the accused as a GPA holder of one G. Laxman. 2004 discloses the existence of building or structure of any kind in the site as on its sale. Therefore, the contention of the accused that, his wife was having rental income from the house in site No.6 to purchase asset No.1 on 09.01.2004 itself is unacceptable. ii) It is not in dispute that, a building with the ground + three floors was constructed at site No.27 in the year 2004 itself. In view of the same, the report of PW6 renders an incomplete. But, his grievance is that, he was a qualified civil engineer. The whole construction of the building was taken place under his self supervision. Therefore, according to him, PW6 should have deducted the construction cost at 10% towards the self supervision and another 10% towards the overhead charges, in all 20% at Rs.2,00,754/-.

With this, his contention is that, the IO should have considered the total construction cost of this building at Rs.8,03,018/- rather than Rs.10,03,772/-. iv) Thus, the difference amount of Rs.2,00,754/- is in dispute. As per the service record of the accused, basically he is an electrical diploma holder and working as the Electrical Engineer even as on the date of raid. No supporting evidence is on record to prove his service on the construction side during the check period. The fact is that, as a public servant, he was to ensure his presence in the 16 Spl. C.C.456/2017 office from morning till evening on all working days. Therefore, the question that arise is, as to how can he invest his official time and supervise the construction of his own buildings?. In fact, the person who undertook the work of construction is competent to speak as to, who has supervised it. But, not examined the said person by the accused. Therefore, I am to discard the defence contention to that extent. The construction of ground + three floors in the area of 15 x 40 sq. ft in the year 2004 at the cost of less than the amount considered by the IO cannot be expected. With these observations, I am to hold that, the cost of construction at Rs.10,03,772/- stands proved. Thus, if the admitted purchase value of Rs.66,000/- if added, would be Rs.10,69,772/-.
